smell: StepDef.ReRunSafe is enforced at declaration time (BuildSteps panics on ReRunSafeUnset) but never consulted at execution time — StepBuilder discards it and Orchestrator.Run never branches on it. The field is decorative metadata that the type system mandates without backing semantics, so a ReRunSafeNo step is treated identically to a ReRunSafeYes step on a partial-fail-and-resume.
severity_reason: declaration-time-only contract creates a false invariant: callers see ReRunSafeNo and assume the orchestrator will guard against rerun, but it does not — the same risk class state-and-recovery flagged as 'decorative' and the recent 1e505e9 commit only widened the surface
fix_summary: Either (a) propagate ReRunSafe into builtStep and have Orchestrator.executeStep skip ReRunSafeNo steps that have no AlreadyDone hook on a recovery rerun, or (b) demote the field to a doc-only label and replace the BuildSteps panic with a //nolint comment + roadmap entry. Today's setup phase has 6 ReRunSafeNo steps with no AlreadyDone — option (a) requires writing those checks; option (b) is honest about the current state.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (StepDef + BuildSteps is the canonical step declaration)
Uber §API Design (don't expose fields the type system enforces but the runtime ignores)
repo-counter-example: AlreadyDoneChecker is a runtime-consulted contract (orchestrator.go:L129-L146)
must_preserve: BuildSteps panic must remain until ReRunSafe is either consumed or removed; do not silently drop it without a roadmap-tracked plan

smell: All five sibling phase constructors take positional (exec, logger, version) args, while their shared base phase.NewBasePhase and the parent okd.New use functional options (WithExecutor/WithLogger/WithVersion, ProvisionerOption). The split forces each phase.New to internally translate positional args into option calls and prevents callers from passing optional knobs (Recorder, Reporter) at construction — they end up writing exported fields directly (okd.go:L138, L147-L148, L156).
fix_summary: Pick one shape for the okd phase family. Recommend functional options (matches NewBasePhase + okd.Provisioner): replace setup/install/postinstall/destroy/cleanup New(exec, logger, version) with New(version, ...PhaseOption) using WithExecutor/WithLogger/WithRecorder/WithReporter shared via phase package. okd.Provisioner.Prepare/Install/etc become single-line forwarders. Net delta ~+15 LOC of option types, -20 LOC of struct-field writes in okd.go.
rule_source: Uber §API Design (sibling constructors should share signature shape)
repo-counter-example: phase.NewBasePhase + okd.New both use ...Option
Go proverb: clear is better than clever (one shape per package family)
must_preserve: phase.NewBasePhase and okd.New (canonical APIs); do not delete WithRecorder

smell: phase.WithRecorder and the install Phase's logutil.NopProgressReporter default exist as functional options on BasePhase, but okd.Provisioner sets them by writing the embedded BasePhase.Recorder field and install.Phase.Reporter field directly (okd.go:L138/L147-L148/L156). Net effect: the option exists, no caller uses it, and the struct fields are intentionally exported to enable post-construction mutation — a hand-written workaround for the option discoverability the constructor is supposed to provide.
evidence:
// okd.go:137
setupPhase := setup.New(p.executor, p.logger, p.version)
setupPhase.Recorder = p.recorder
setupPhase.BinDir = phase.ResolveBinDir(cfg)
...
// install:
installPhase.Recorder = p.recorder
installPhase.Reporter = p.reporter
fix_summary: Either thread Recorder/Reporter into each phase.New as functional options (matches the api:beabab0c fix) and drop the public Recorder/Reporter fields, or remove phase.WithRecorder since nothing calls it. Don't ship both. If WithRecorder stays for a future caller, document the future usage in MEMORY.md §scaffolding so the next audit recognises it.
rule_source: Uber §API Design
Go Style Guide §Mutability (don't expose mutable fields when constructor options exist)
repo-counter-example: phase.WithRecorder defined but unreferenced (paths.go:L153)

smell: download.Options, download.ExtractOptions, and cleanup.Options pass an optional *slog.Logger as a struct field with a getter (o.logger() / opts.getLogger()), while every sibling — executor.WithLogger, terraform.WithLogger, proxmox.WithLogger, addon.WithLogger, cluster.WithLogger, phase.WithLogger — uses functional options. The struct-field shape forces every Download/Extract/cleanup call site to allocate a struct-with-pointer and routes nil through a getter, while the option shape has logutil.OrNop applied once at construction.
fix_summary: Either (a) commit the codebase to options-struct everywhere — uniform but loses at-construction nil-normalisation; or (b) commit to functional options — replace download.Download(ctx, *Options) with download.Fetch(ctx, url, dst string, opts ...Option). Recommend (b): three of the four call sites set ≤2 fields, so the per-call-site delta is small and matches the prevailing pattern. cleanup.Options stays a struct (its fields are required workdir/path data, not optional knobs) but Logger should move to a functional WithLogger.
rule_source: Uber §API Design
Go Style Guide §Function Argument Lists
repo-counter-example: every other internal package uses functional options for *slog.Logger
must_preserve: download retry/checksum guarantees and cleanup BaseOptions struct embedding

smell: PhaseContext[T].Update takes a func(*T) under a write lock, with a doc warning that fn must not call Get or Update on the same PhaseContext because sync.RWMutex is not reentrant. That's a footgun on an exported public API: caller closures can transitively reach Get through any helper that takes the same context, deadlocking the orchestrator. Zero value is constructible (var c PhaseContext[T]) but the no-reentrancy invariant is unenforceable beyond a doc comment.
fix_summary: Either (a) make NewPhaseContext required by panicking on a sentinel zero value and surface the no-reentrancy invariant on the Update method itself rather than buried in a doc comment; or (b) accept zero-value usability and switch to a sync.Mutex with a callback-only API that returns the new value (no nested-call deadlock if fn is a pure transform). Today's only consumer (postinstall) goes through NewPhaseContext, so (a) is cheap.
rule_source: Go Style Guide §Zero Value (zero values should be useful or panic clearly)
CLAUDE.md §code-comments (subtle invariants and footguns warrant comments) — but invariants better expressed in types
must_preserve: PhaseContext API; only one consumer today

smell: executor.WithInheritedEnv has no callers in the production tree — every executor.New call goes through WithEnv, WithWorkDir, or WithLogger. The function exists as a documented escape hatch ('a tool that consumes a variable not on the allowlist') but no such tool currently exists.
fix_summary: Verify intent. WithInheritedEnv is shaped like a symmetric API to WithEnv — keep under MEMORY.md §scaffolding. If the doctor or debug-bundle tooling will eventually need to spawn a process with the full env (e.g. a wrapper that consumes NO_PROXY in a custom form), promote that intent in roadmap.md so the next audit recognises it.
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric-API shape stays)
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (executor is the canonical subprocess runner)

smell: phase.BinDirOrDefault is a 6-line helper consumed by 3 sibling sites (setup/artifacts.go, setup/tools.go, cleanup/packages.go). Together with PreflightBinDir and ResolveBinDir it forms a three-function bin-dir-resolution surface; each function differs only in which input source is consulted. The shape is correct (small symmetric API) but BinDirOrDefault is invoked on a struct field that's already populated by ResolveBinDir at construction — the second call is redundant defense.
fix_summary: Either (a) keep BinDirOrDefault as scaffolding for future bin-dir resolution callers (status, doctor, debug-bundle) — it's already symmetric with PreflightBinDir/ResolveBinDir; or (b) inline the 3 call sites since they all read p.BinDir which ResolveBinDir already populates with a non-empty value. (a) is the safer call and matches the canonical-helper pattern.
rule_source: MEMORY.md §scaffolding (symmetric-api stays)
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (phase package is the canonical helper home)

smell: config.Loader is a stateless struct (zero fields). NewLoader returns &Loader{}, LoadFile and Save read no state. Six call sites — cli/deploy.go, cli/helpers.go, cli/doctor.go (twice) — all do loader := config.NewLoader(); loader.LoadFile(p), the no-state equivalent of two package-level functions LoadFile and Save.
fix_summary: Either (a) collapse Loader into package-level config.LoadFile / config.Save functions (5 call sites become 1-line each instead of 2-line); or (b) give Loader at least one field (e.g., a strict-mode flag, an extra-validators slice) so the struct earns its keep. Today the type is a placeholder shaped like 'we'll add fields later' — fine if (b) is on the roadmap, otherwise (a). Six refactor sites, all in cli/, low merge-conflict risk.
rule_source: Go Style Guide §Receiver vs Function
Uber §Initialism (constructor exists only when there's state to initialize)
must_preserve: yaml.UnmarshalStrict + permission check + schemaVersion gate (LoadFile invariants)

smell: NewK8sClient reads os.Getenv(KUBECONFIG) and runs executor.CommandExists(oc) inside the constructor. Both side effects make zero-value construction (var c cluster.K8sClient) produce a non-equivalent object, and the env probe leaks into tests. The install phase already documents this hazard (install/phase.go:L162-L165: K8sClient reads os.Environ at construction and will NOT see this — callers must pass cluster.WithKubeconfig explicitly).
fix_summary: Move the env-var read and CommandExists probe into a separate WithDefaults() option (or a default-applying helper invoked only when no WithCLI/WithKubeconfig is supplied). Better still, accept the kubeconfig path as a required arg to NewK8sClient (config-driven, not env-driven) and have callers explicitly pass cluster.WithKubeconfigFromEnv when they want env fallback. The install phase's SetupKubeconfig already warns about exactly this gotcha.
rule_source: Go Style Guide §Constructor (constructors should not have observable side effects beyond initialization)
Uber §Side Effects
repo-counter-example: install.Phase.SetupKubeconfig has a doc comment warning about exactly this hazard

smell: runlock.Lock has a single unexported pointer field f *os.File. The zero value (Lock{}) is constructible by callers (var l runlock.Lock) but Release would nil-deref on l.f.Name(). Acquire is the only constructor and returns *Lock — the type doesn't enforce that.
fix_summary: Add a nil-and-zero guard at the top of Release: if l == nil || l.f == nil { return }. Cheap, makes the zero-value safe-but-no-op. Net delta +3 LOC. Alternative: panic with a clear message on the zero value if you want to enforce constructor-only construction.
rule_source: Go Style Guide §Zero Value
Uber §API Design (pointer-receiver methods on a type whose constructor returns *T should nil-guard)

smell: version package exports five mutable package-level variables (Version, GitCommit, BuildDate, GoVersion, Platform). They are intended to be set once via -ldflags at build time but the type system permits any caller to write to them at runtime, racing with version.BackgroundCheck which reads Version. The package doc mentions ldflags but doesn't enforce the immutability.
evidence:
var (
	Version   = "0.1.0"
	GitCommit = "unknown"
	BuildDate = "unknown"
	GoVersion = runtime.Version()
	Platform  = fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s", runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
)
fix_summary: Either (a) accept the convention — every Go binary uses ldflags this way and var is the canonical shape; or (b) introduce unexported buildVersion / buildCommit and exported getter functions Version() / Commit() that snapshot the build vars under a sync.Once. (a) is the prevailing Go pattern; (b) is more correct but heavier. Recommend (a) plus a comment forbidding writes from non-test callers.
rule_source: Go Style Guide §Immutable
Go convention: ldflags injection uses var blocks

smell: cleanup package ships two Execute entry points: a method (p *Phase) Execute(ctx, *Options) and a package-level Execute(ctx, *Options). The method is a one-line forwarder to the package func. Three callers consume the package func directly (destroy/steps.go via cleanup.New(...).Execute, okd.go:L132 via the same pattern, and tests). The dual surface forces callers to choose, and the comment 'mirrors the shape of setup/install/postinstall/destroy' (cleanup.go:L57) explicitly admits the method exists for symmetry, not for use.
fix_summary: Pick one shape. Either (a) collapse to a single package-level cleanup.Execute(ctx, opts) and remove cleanup.Phase + cleanup.New (callers in okd.go:L132 and destroy/steps.go:L117 already accept the function-only form); or (b) keep cleanup.Phase as the canonical surface for symmetry with setup/install/postinstall/destroy and unexport the package-level Execute. (b) matches the comment's intent and the api:beabab0c sibling-shape preference; the dual surface is what's wrong, not which one stays.
rule_source: Uber §API Design (one canonical entry point per operation)
Go proverb: clear is better than clever
CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes (canonical APIs should be single-shape)
must_preserve: cleanup.Kind enum and its sub-step ordering
